draft.title: Limits of each criterion
card: Each way of judging behaviour has a weakness. That is why a single test is not enough to decide if behaviour is typical.
behaviour that few people show is not always a problem. Being a gifted musician is rare, and it is healthy.
norms differ between cultures and change over time. A behaviour can be accepted in one place or decade and not in another.
some conditions cause little distress to the person, and distress can be a normal reaction, such as grief. Whether behaviour is maladaptive depends on the person and their situation.
draft.remember: Every criterion can mislead on its own, so psychologists weigh several together.

a.q: Why is statistical rarity a weak test of whether behaviour is atypical?
opts: Rare behaviour can be healthy, such as great musical talent
Rare behaviour is always caused by a mental health condition
Common behaviour is never a sign of a problem
Rare behaviour is never noticed by other people
a.why: Statistical rarity only counts how uncommon a behaviour is, not whether it is harmful. Talent is rare and healthy, so rarity alone cannot show a problem. The option saying rare behaviour always signals a condition reverses this.
a.clue: Think about a rare skill that helps a person.

b.q: In Mei's country, it is polite to greet elders by bowing. Visiting another country, she is told that bowing seems odd. Which weakness of judging by social norms does this show?
opts: Norms are always set by a small group
Norms only apply to rare behaviour
b.why: The same bow is polite in one culture and odd in another, so judging by one set of norms can give a wrong result. The option saying norms cannot change is wrong, as the card says norms change across cultures and over time.
b.clue: The same behaviour is judged differently in two places.

a.best: Rare behaviour can be healthy, such as great musical talent

a.q: Why is statistical rarity, on its own, a weak test of whether behaviour is atypical?
opts: It counts how uncommon a behaviour is, not whether it harms
It treats common behaviour as a likely sign of a problem
It relies on how upset the person feels about the behaviour
It judges behaviour by whether it helps the person cope
